title: India Rout Pakistan 19-0 to Storm Into Junior Women's Hockey Asia Cup Semis
excerpt: India's junior women thrashed Pakistan 19-0 in their Women's Junior Asia Cup quarterfinal in Moqi, China — Pooja Malik hit a hat-trick and the defending champions, now two wins from a third straight continental title, face the South Korea-Malaysia winner in the semifinals.
body:
• India thrashed Pakistan 19-0 in their 2026 Women's Junior Asia Cup quarterfinal in Moqi, China, on Thursday, storming into the semifinals.
  • Pooja Malik scored a hat-trick, while Sanika Mane, Supriya, Madhu Sidar, Purnima Yadav and Roshni Aind each scored twice; India led 10-0 at half-time.
  • The defending champions have now scored 41 goals in five matches at the tournament, having topped their group with wins over Japan, Malaysia and South Korea.
  • India, winners of the title in 2023 and 2024, are two wins from a hat-trick of Junior Women's Asia Cup crowns and will face the winner of South Korea vs Malaysia in the semifinal on September 12.

A record-margin demolition

India produced one of the most emphatic victories in Women's Junior Asia Cup history on Thursday, dismantling Pakistan 19-0 in their quarterfinal in Moqi, China, to move within two wins of a third successive continental title. The defending champions needed only seven minutes to break the deadlock, with Puja Sahoo finding the net, and Roshni Aind doubled the advantage two minutes later, according to IANS.

What followed was a relentless assault. India added four more goals in the next five minutes — Tanushree Dinesh Kadu and Sukhveer Kaur struck in the 11th and 13th minutes, with Sanika Mane also scoring in the 13th. Madhu Sidar and Geeta Yadav extended the lead before Mane grabbed her second in the 23rd minute. Tanuja Toppo and Pooja Malik completed the first-half scoring, and Purnima Yadav's 33rd-minute strike took India into the interval with a staggering 10-0 lead.

There was no let-up after the restart. Sidar scored again in the 39th minute, Supriya opened her account a minute later, and Malik took centre stage with goals in the 49th and 51st minutes to complete her hat-trick. Krishna Sharma and Binima Dhan added further strikes, Supriya scored again in the 54th minute, and Aind capped the rout with her second goal in the final minute.

Defending champions at full throttle

The 19-goal haul was the culmination of a dominant tournament so far. India topped their group with victories over Japan, Malaysia and South Korea, and have now scored 41 goals in five matches while conceding almost nothing of note. They won this title in 2023 and 2024; the margin against Pakistan underscores how far ahead of the rest of the continent this generation is.

It has been a golden week for Indian junior hockey overall. The men's team also marched into the semifinals of their Asia Cup: Anmol Ekka's six-goal blitz powered India into the last four of the AHF Junior Asia Cup, and the men's side beat Chinese Taipei to seal their semifinal berth, according to Sportstar. The Hockey India development pipeline is delivering on both fronts simultaneously.

What the scoreline says

India–Pakistan is the most storied rivalry in Asian hockey, which makes a 19-0 scoreline startling even by junior standards. The gap reflects two realities: India's structured junior program, with regular exposure to top-level competition and a clear pathway to the senior squad, and Pakistan's struggles to field a competitive junior women's setup. For India, the concern will be the opposite one — staying sharp and match-hardened when the opposition offers so little resistance before a likely tougher semifinal against South Korea or Malaysia, both teams India have already beaten in the group stage.

Diaspora angle

Field hockey is growing quietly in the diaspora — junior leagues in Canada, the US and the UK now feature Indian-origin players in meaningful numbers. This India side offers them a direct point of connection: several of these players are teenagers who will be in contention for the senior national team within a year or two. A third straight Asia Cup title would give diaspora hockey academies a ready-made set of role models to point to.

What's next

India await the winner of the South Korea–Malaysia quarterfinal, with the semifinal scheduled for September 12. The final would follow shortly after. Hockey India's official account celebrated the quarterfinal win on social media, and the junior women's team will know the job is only two-thirds done — a hat-trick of titles, not a 19-0 scoreline, is the prize they came for.
